title: Argument Map
instructions: Build a clear 3-level argument map: (1) one central thesis as the root claim, (2) 2–4 distinctly named support reasons as bridge nodes — each describing a different pillar of the argument, (3) specific evidence quotes as leaf nodes attached beneath their relevant support reason. In each chunk, select short verbatim quotes that reveal the author’s concrete positions, causal evidence, or key data points. During synthesis, assign each quote to exactly one named support pillar and list its quote IDs inline on that pillar’s numbered line. The final graph must show a clear, navigable hierarchy: thesis → named reasons → evidence.

title: Methodology Tracker
instructions: Build a structured map of how the document's methodology works. Identify the overarching method or approach as a finding node (the 'what'), then 2–4 method steps as bridge nodes ordered by phase (design → collection → processing → analysis → validation). Attach specific evidence quotes beneath each step to prove that step was actually used or described. Show how steps produce findings using 'produces' relations. Each step must be distinctly named with its actual role — never use generic names like 'Step 1' or 'Method'.

title: Relationship / Network Tracker
instructions: Build a map of how people and organizations in the document connect, collaborate, affiliate with, or oppose each other. Identify key person_org nodes as bridges, backed by quote evidence proving their connections. Produce a central finding node summarizing the overall network dynamic or power structure. Each person_org must have a meaningful name (never 'Author' or 'Researcher'). Every relationship edge must be backed by at least one quote. Capture affiliations, collaborations, and oppositions using their specific relation types.

title: Timeline Tracker
instructions: Build a chronological map of key events described in the document. Identify 2–4 named time periods as top-level containers, then place specific timeline_event nodes within each period showing what happened. Attach quote evidence to each event proving it occurred. Show causal chains using 'led_to' relations where one event triggered another. Produce a central finding node summarizing the overall trajectory or arc. Event names must be specific and descriptive — never 'Event 1' or 'Occurrence'. Time period names must reflect their actual era or phase.
